name: Dev Orus 1.1 — Complete Python Course
scope: Python only. C and C++ are deliberately excluded until the Python final assessment is passed.
teaching_policy: Use the complete and advanced reference materials as one integrated curriculum, not one tiny lesson per conversation. Teach explanations, runnable examples, expected outputs, edge cases, exercises, worked solutions, debugging and unseen evaluation. Do not mark mastery from reading or retrieval alone.
completion_policy: Python is complete only after all modules and capstone projects are covered and the learner passes a cumulative unseen assessment. Dataset records and retrieval examples are not neural weight training.

modules.title: Python overview, use cases, implementation and language versions
Installing Python, interpreter, REPL, scripts, PATH and running files
Syntax, statements, expressions, indentation, comments and docstrings
Names, variables, assignment, identity and naming conventions
Built-in scalar types: int, float, complex, bool and NoneType
Numeric operators, precedence, floor division, modulo and exponentiation
Strings, indexing, slicing, Unicode, methods and formatting
Type conversion, truthiness, equality, identity and comparison chaining
Boolean logic, short-circuit evaluation and conditional expressions
if, elif, else, match/case and structural pattern matching
while, for, range, enumerate, zip, break, continue and loop else
Lists, tuples, sequence operations, slicing and copying
Dictionaries, sets, membership, hashing and mapping operations
Comprehensions and generator expressions
Functions, definition, calling, return, docstrings and annotations
Positional, keyword, default, variadic and keyword-only parameters
Argument unpacking, scope, LEGB, closures and global/nonlocal
Recursion, base cases, recursion limits and iterative alternatives
Lambda, map, filter, sorted and key functions
Modules, imports, import search path and __name__
Packages, __init__, relative imports and project layouts
Standard library tour: pathlib, os, sys, math, statistics, random, datetime
Exceptions, exception hierarchy, raise, try/except/else/finally and custom exceptions
File I/O, text/binary modes, encodings, buffering and pathlib
Context managers, with, contextlib and resource cleanup
JSON, CSV, serialization and data validation
Regular expressions with re
Iterables, iterators, iterator protocol and StopIteration
Generators, yield, yield from, lazy evaluation and generator pipelines
Decorators, closures, functools.wraps and parameterized decorators
Object-oriented programming, classes, instances, attributes and methods
Constructors, __init__, __new__, representation and comparison dunder methods
Encapsulation conventions, properties, descriptors and attribute lookup
Inheritance, overriding, super, MRO and multiple inheritance
Composition, protocols, abstract base classes and duck typing
Dataclasses, enums, slots and object model trade-offs
Type hints, typing, unions, generics, Protocol and static checking
Virtual environments, pip, dependency pinning and reproducible installs
Project packaging, pyproject.toml, wheels and entry points
Unit testing with unittest, test discovery, fixtures and mocks
Debugging, tracebacks, pdb, logging and diagnostics
Code quality, formatting, linting, documentation and maintainability
Networking fundamentals and HTTP clients with standard library concepts
Databases, sqlite3, transactions, parameterized queries and data integrity
Concurrency models: threads, processes, GIL and when to use each
Async programming: asyncio, coroutines, tasks, cancellation and timeouts
Performance measurement, profiling, algorithmic complexity and memory
Robust input validation, secure file handling, secrets and safe subprocess use
Data structures and algorithms implemented in Python
Capstone: tested command-line utility, file processor and small application
Final assessment: unseen code reading, writing, debugging and design tasks

assessment.mastery: At least 80% on the module assessment, with all critical correctness and safety checks passing; retry weak topics before advancing.
assessment.final: Mixed unseen tasks covering syntax, data model, control flow, functions, collections, files, exceptions, OOP, iterators, typing, testing, concurrency and application design.
